SpringSocial: Social Skills App for ADHD & Autistic Adults

# Build Better Social Skills in a Safe Practice Space

Neurodivergent-friendly social skills practice app

SpringSocial lets you practise real-world social situations on your own device, with no account, no cloud sync and no judgment. Explore 1,000 scenarios designed for autistic, ADHD and anxious adults who want clearer, calmer conversations.

 No accounts or logins No personal data collection No account required 

## What You Can Practise in SpringSocial

### Work, friendships, family & more

Practise realistic situations like speaking up in meetings, joining a conversation, handling feedback, reconnecting with friends, or navigating awkward family moments.

### See how your choices land

Every choice comes with friendly feedback that explains why some responses help and others might cause confusion or tension — especially useful if “unwritten rules” have never been clear.

### Practice stays on your device

SpringSocial doesn’t require an account or store your responses on a server. You can experiment freely, make mistakes and learn at your own pace.

## How SpringSocial Works

1

### Choose a scenario

Pick from 1,000 scenarios covering work, study, friendships, dating, family and everyday interactions.

2

### Make your choices

At each step, you choose how you’d respond and watch the interaction unfold based on your decisions.

### Read the feedback

After each choice, you’ll see clear, non-judgmental feedback

# SocialWise: LLM-Agentic Conversation Therapy for Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder to Enhance Communication Skills

Albert Tang

(2025)

###### Abstract.

Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) affects more than 75 million people worldwide. However, scalable support for practicing everyday conversation is scarce: Low-cost activities such as story reading yield limited improvement. At the same time, effective role-play therapy demands expensive, in-person sessions with specialists. SocialWise bridges this gap through a browser-based application that pairs LLM conversational agents with a therapeutic retrieval augmented generation (RAG) knowledge base. Users select a scenario (e.g., ordering food, joining a group), interact by text or voice, and receive instant, structured feedback on tone, engagement, and alternative phrasing. The SocialWise prototype, implemented with Streamlit, LangChain, and ChromaDB, runs on any computer with internet access, and demonstrates how recent advances in LLM can provide evidence-based, on-demand communication coaching for individuals with ASD.
